claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To get started, I need to gather some information about your situation. Let me begin with a few key questions.

**First, could you please tell me: How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child. His name is Alex and he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, the main eligibility rules would apply. Let me ask you the next question:

**Are you responsible for Alex? Specifically, do you live with him, or are you paying towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for Alex. He lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. Since Alex lives with you, that's an important part of the eligibility criteria.

**Next, I need to ask: Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's another key requirement met.

Now I have a few more questions to ensure there are no other circumstances affecting your eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any form of residential accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has actually been in hospital for a while now - about 3 to 4 months or so. But I still visit him regularly and buy him things like clothes, books, and his favorite snacks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail that affects your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me, Alex has been in hospital for 3 to 4 months. According to the Child Benefit rules, if a child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you would normally no longer be entitled to Child Benefit.

However, there is a potential exception: **if you regularly spend money on the child while they're in hospital, you may still be eligible.**

You've mentioned that you visit regularly and buy things like clothes, books, and snacks for Alex. This sounds like you are making regular contributions to his upkeep.

**To help me assess this fully, could you tell me: Are these purchases (clothes, books, snacks, etc.) something you do on a regular basis - for example, weekly or several times a month?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I visit him several times a week and I'm always bringing him things he needs or enjoys - new clothes when he needs them, magazines and books to keep him entertained, and his favorite treats and snacks. It's regular spending, not just occasional.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detailed information. That's very helpful.

Based on everything you've told me, let me now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Your situation:**
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- You are responsible for Alex and he lives with you ✓
- Alex is currently in hospital (over 12 weeks)
- You regularly spend money on Alex's upkeep (visiting several times a week, buying clothes, books, snacks, and treats)

According to the Child Benefit rules, while children in hospital for more than 12 weeks would normally make you ineligible, there is an exception: **if you regularly spend money on them, you can continue to receive Child Benefit.**

Your regular contributions towards Alex's clothes, books, entertainment, and treats clearly demonstrate ongoing financial support for his upkeep, which qualifies you for this exception.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Conclusion: You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Your regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep while he's in hospital qualify you for the exception to the normal 12-week limit. Make sure you continue to keep records of your spending on Alex's behalf, as this evidence of your regular contributions is important.

If you haven't already done so, you may want to contact HMRC (Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs) to inform them of Alex's hospital stay and your circumstances, so they have the full picture of your situation on file.
